key_insight: Interface orientation tunes heat transfer in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures, with extrapolated infinite-length thermal conductance higher for armchair interfaces (473 MW/m²K) than zigzag interfaces (387 MW/m²K).
engineering_relevance: Choosing armchair interfaces could improve heat dissipation in lateral TMD nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.
method: Train a DeePMD-kit deep learning interatomic potential on DFT data.
Use non-equilibrium molecular dynamics to compare armchair and zigzag interfaces.
Simulate 10–40 nm cells and extrapolate conductance to infinite length.
evidence_signal: The potential closely matches DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersions; armchair conductance is higher at every simulated length, with greater phonon spectral overlap at 300 K.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based results but no experimental validation, leaving performance in fabricated interfaces uncertain.
paper_title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
